newsitem.title: ITALY: War of words in Italian metalworker dispute.
newsitem.headline: War of words in Italian metalworker dispute.

text.p: Labour Minister Tiziano Treu said on Thursday that talks must resume to end the long-running dispute in the Italian metalworker and engineering sector as unions and management continued to wage a war of words.
Negotiations over the renewal of contracts for some 1.7 million workers stalled last year and employers' federation Federmeccanica has since rejected government suggestions for a settlement.
"We are in a difficult position, but we have to carry on working because this contract has to be completed," Treu told reporters at a political convention.
Unions lashed Federmeccanica for dismissing government proposals that workers should be given a 200,000 ($129) a month pay rise to cover the 1996-98 contract period.
Unions, who originally asked for 230,000 lire, have accepted the proposal but management has stuck to its 139,000 lire offer.

"The metalworkers have been forced to follow the path of a tough battle which we had hoped could be abandoned," said Pietro Larizza, leader of the UIL union. "Federmeccanica has clearly discovered class struggle."
Giorgio Fossa, head of the general employers' organisation Confindustria, said the government suggestion was inflationary but added that other proposals might be put on the table.
"We hope to be able to conclude this contract as soon as possible, in the coming weeks, because there are new, possible solutions to end the dispute," Fossa said.
However Sergio Cofferati, head of Italy's largest union, the Cigl, rejected talk of new proposals. "For us (only) the government proposal remains. Nothing has changed," he said.
Unions have called a 10-hour strike to be held on a factory-by-factory basis between today and January 25.
It is the third major strike called by unions in the six-month dispute.
